Learn to explain giving objects what they need: Dependency, Dependency Injection & Constructor Injection, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Dependency - An object that another object needs in order to do its work.
Dependency Injection - A technique where an object receives what it needs from outside instead of creating it.
Constructor Injection - A form of injection where you pass the needed objects into the initializer.

Dependency - An object that another object needs in order to do its work.
한국어: Dependency: 다른 객체가 일하기 위해 필요로 하는 객체

Dependency Injection - A technique where an object receives what it needs from outside instead of creating it.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Dependency, Dependency Injection and Constructor Injection in English?

dialogue.title: Hard to test

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our old `Cart` created its own `Logger` inside, so tests are hard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The `Logger` is a dependency of `Cart`. It needs it to work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So a dependency is just an object that another object needs?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Now use dependency injection: give the object what it needs from outside.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like in this code, where `Cart` receives `logger` in its `init`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, that is constructor injection. You pass the dependency into the initializer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then you cannot swap it in a test. Dependency injection lets you pass a fake one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is constructor injection safer than setting a property later?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The object is ready as soon as it exists.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. I will inject every dependency in our view models.
The network client is a dependency of this view model.
